question.problem:
Which of the three sequences below are arithmetic sequences?

I. $6,10,14,18,...$

II. $4,8,16,32,...$

III. $87,74,61,46,...$
question.worked_solution:
To determine whether each sequence is an arithmetic sequence, we need to look at the jumps between terms in the sequence. If the jumps are the same, then they indeed represent a common difference of an arithmetic sequence.

- In sequence I, the jumps are all the same. Therefore, sequence I is an arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/bbb6555443ed4fdf7f29da4571d421b833fb21e2556a440d821bbd4e4b986923.png)

- In sequence II, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence II is not an arithmetic sequence.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/6408dd510dd59615c69c063897a6ff483c20bc485d73164e74c2f57dacc4dce8.png)

- In sequence III, the jumps are not all the same. Therefore, sequence III is not an arithmetic sequence.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14203588/assets/246210488611eed52df8d3e777e296bff30889c7dd8122d082c5d4a6bb6d7ad6.png)

In conclusion, only sequence I is an arithmetic sequence.
